newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines eyes limit on real estate loans.
newsitem.headline: Philippines eyes limit on real estate loans.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank is studying the possibility of limiting loan exposures of banks on the real estate industry, saying recent expansion of loans to the sector could build up inflationary pressures.

The bank's Department of Economic Research, in a study released on Thursday, proposed the monetary authorities "prescribe a single industry exposure limit equivalent to 50 percent of the banks' net worth."
Other recommendations include setting up an allowance for probable losses equivalent to 25 percent of the loans, and continued close monitoring of banks' loan to the sector.

The department study said recent expansion of loans in the industry "has raised certain policy concerns because the underlying speculative demand for real estate could lead to a possible build-up of inflationary pressures."
A slowdown of the sector could lead to costly financial adjustments and restructuring of banks which have heavy exposure, it added.
The study, however, showed that credits to real estate projects were at an average of 9.2 percent of the total loan portfolio of banks.
The bank's policy-making Monetary Board has yet to act on the recommendations.
